question: What is the primary goal of workplace ergonomics in a clinical environment?

options.A: Reducing hospital financial expenditures on furniture
options.B: Adapting tasks and equipment to fit human physical capabilities
options.C: Eliminating the need for physical breaks during work hours
options.D: Speeding up electronic documentation processes during shifts

explanation: Ergonomics focuses on fitting the work environment and tools to the worker to enhance safety and efficiency. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h1)

question: Why are administrative and documentation tasks considered a significant ergonomic concern for modern healthcare workers?

options.A: They require constant heavy lifting of paper patient records
options.B: They eliminate the need for any physical movement during shifts
options.C: They involve prolonged static postures and repetitive micro-movements
options.D: They expose personnel to hazardous chemical sterilizing agents

explanation: Desk and computer work forces the body to maintain fixed positions for extended periods, straining muscles and joints. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h1)

question: What happens to the effective physical load on the cervical spine when the head is tilted forward during screen use?

options.A: The cervical spine bones decrease in overall density
options.B: The muscular load transfers completely to the lower extremities
options.C: The effective load increases significantly due to leverage
options.D: The effective load remains entirely unchanged

explanation: Forward head posture creates a mechanical lever effect, dramatically multiplying the weight force experienced by neck vertebrae and supporting muscles. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h2)

question: How do supporting muscles react when a static, poor posture is maintained over several hours of electronic charting?

options.A: They enter a state of continuous, fatiguing contraction
options.B: They experience complete muscular relaxation and rest
options.C: They automatically increase in structural length and volume
options.D: They cease all metabolic activity to conserve cellular energy

explanation: Static loading deprives muscle fibers of intermittent relaxation phases, leading to rapid fatigue, reduced blood flow, and localized discomfort. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h2)

question: Which medical condition involves the compression of the median nerve inside the wrist due to repetitive typing or poor hand positioning?
explanation: Carpal tunnel syndrome occurs when the median nerve is squeezed as it passes through the narrow wrist canal, often aggravated by repetitive hand motions and poor wrist angles. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h3)

question: A staff member who spends entire shifts typing medical notes with unsupported wrists and elevated shoulders is most likely to develop which disorder?
explanation: Elevated shoulders and unsupported arms place continuous strain on the upper trapezius and neck muscles, resulting in tension neck syndrome. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h3)

question: Where should the top of a computer monitor be positioned relative to the user's face?

options.A: Significantly higher than the top of the head
options.B: At or slightly below eye level
options.C: Parallel to the chest sternum level
options.D: Directly aligned with the top of the forehead

explanation: Placing the top of the screen at or just below eye level encourages a neutral neck posture, preventing the user from looking up or straining downward. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h4)

question: What is the correct angle for a user's elbows when typing at an electronic health record terminal?

options.C: Compressed tightly against the ribs at 45 degrees
options.D: Lifted upward level with the shoulders

explanation: Keeping elbows bent at approximately a right angle allows forearms to rest comfortably and reduces shoulder strain while interacting with the keyboard. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h4)

question: Which action helps reduce physical strain when operating mobile computer carts in clinical wards?

options.A: Attaching extra equipment to the top shelf to increase momentum
options.B: Ensuring caster wheels are well-maintained to avoid excessive pushing force
options.C: Pushing the heavy cart rapidly using only one outstretched arm
options.D: Looking downward at the screen while navigating crowded hallways

explanation: Stuck or damaged wheels increase the force required to move carts, placing sudden stress on the lumbar spine and upper extremities. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h5)

question: What is the recommended body posture when reviewing clinical data on a handheld tablet at a patient's bedside?

options.A: Extending arms fully outward to keep the screen far from the eyes
options.B: Keeping the device close to the core body line with a neutral neck
options.C: Tilting the head sharply downward to focus solely on the device
options.D: Holding the tablet with a tight one-handed grip for stability

explanation: Keeping devices close to the body reduces lever stress on the arms and prevents unnecessary forward bending of the neck. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h5)

question: What does the twenty-twenty-twenty rule recommend for preventing digital eye strain?

options.A: Every 20 minutes, look at something 20 feet away for 20 seconds
options.B: Every 20 hours, rest the eyes for 20 minutes in a dark room
options.C: Every 20 seconds, adjust the screen brightness up by 20 percent
options.D: Every 20 minutes, blink 20 times rapidly while closing both eyes

explanation: This simple rule gives the focusing muscles inside the eyes a chance to relax and refocus away from close-up digital displays. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h6)

question: How should a computer terminal be oriented relative to a window to minimize screen glare?

options.A: Flat on the floor beneath the window sill
options.D: With the window directly behind the screen

explanation: Placing the monitor perpendicular to light sources prevents direct glare on the screen and harsh light shining directly into the user's eyes. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h6)

question: What is the primary physiological benefit of taking short micro-breaks during long charting sessions?

options.A: Increasing systemic blood pressure to normal baseline levels
options.B: Eliminating all future risk of occupational burnout
options.C: Permanently reversing existing spinal disc degeneration
options.D: Restoring microcirculation to fatigued muscle fibers

explanation: Static postures restrict blood flow; brief pauses and movement allow blood to circulate back into tense muscles, delivering oxygen and removing waste products. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT an appropriate time or method to integrate ergonomic micro-breaks into a clinical shift?

options.A: Taking a 30-second neck rotation break between patient admissions
options.B: Doing shoulder rolls while waiting for a software screen to load
options.C: Performing wrist flexor stretches during a brief pause in documentation
options.D: Waiting until the end of a 12-hour shift to do all stretching at once

explanation: Waiting until the shift ends defeats the purpose of micro-breaks, which are designed to periodically relieve strain throughout the working day before damage accumulates. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h7)
